thread.title: Apple Stock Downgraded; iPhone Seen 'Hitting A Plateau'

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Downgraded; iPhone Seen 'Hitting A Plateau'
text:
A Wall Street firm on Wednesday downgraded Apple ( AAPL ) stock and slashed its price target on concerns that the iPhone maker is "hitting a plateau."
BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long lowered his rating on Apple to market perform, or neutral, from outperform and cut his price target to 162 from 199.
X Apple shares added 0.3% to close at 167.43 on the stock market today . Apple is trading below its 50-day moving average, a negative technical indicator. Apple has tumbled about 7% since hitting an all-time high of 180.10 on Jan. 18.
"There has been much in the press about order cuts for iPhone X, and we believe a weaker mix in Q1 will push estimates lower for March and beyond," Long said in a report. "We are more concerned by a secular change for iPhone. Following 10 years where (average selling prices) have generally moved higher, we believe prices will plateau as with the rest of the industry."
Long also expects Apple to see no growth year over year in the China market, a reversal from last quarter's 12% growth after six quarters of double-digit declines.
Apple is scheduled to report December-quarter results after the market close Thursday.
Long believes Apple's March-quarter guidance will be "well below current consensus."
"We still view the iPhone base as growing, and the devices are on average getting older," Long said. "However, without a compelling product cycle in September, we may see a slow upgrade cycle once again."
Consumers were excited about the launch of the iPhone X because it featured an OLED display, facial recognition security and augmented reality technology. But the fall 2018 iPhones aren't looking very compelling, he said.
